column1: # Rows db.sw.* (line PS-SW, 2026-11-26; fix round 1, 2026-11-27): PSIBLAST -use_sw_tback (NCBI's Smith-Waterman redo, blast_traceback.c:1486-1487, blast_hspstream.c:678-686, redo_alignment.c:1310-1555), frozen from NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0 at -num_threads 1 (the rows of fix round 1 from the official Linux build): round 1 (the square matrix), the PSSM rounds (-num_iterations 2, 3, 0/convergence, -in_pssm, a PSSM of scores only, -in_msa), -comp_based_stats 0 to 3 (scale 1 and the redo in OID order at 0), -sum_stats true, -db and -subject, -phi_pattern, -matrix IDENTITY, gap-leading SW alignments (swgap), outfmt 0, 5, 6, 7 and 11, the PSSM files (-out_pssm, -out_ascii_pssm, -save_each_pssm), a CBS 0 heap that fills (acbs, -max_target_seqs 1), inputs whose SW bytes differ from the X-drop redo's (sicy, inpssm.tkxbz, inpssm.lcq), and the failed, crashing, endless and fetch-excluded boundaries in round 1 and in the PSSM rounds (x4, x4excl and pssw inputs; PD-LOSAT-NCBI-DEFECTS 1.123); the check runs them at 1 and 4 threads. Freeze them alone with db_search_fixtures.py freeze --ncbi-bin DIR --program psiblast --only db.sw.
